newsitem.title: USA: Guidant Q1 cardiac rhythm sales strong.
newsitem.headline: Guidant Q1 cardiac rhythm sales strong.

text.p: Guidant Corp posted solid first-quarter gains in cardiac rhythm management and minimally invasive systems sales, but vascular intervention systems sales trends remained weak.
The medical devices maker said Monday that, after currency effects, vascular intervention sales declined 5.7 percent to $100.8 million on the quarter ended March 31.
Cardiac rhythm management sales rose 11 percent to $149 million, and minimally invasive systems sales rose 38 percent to $15.7 million, Guidant said.
Shares in Guidant were off 1-1/8 to 58-3/4.
Total sales including all business lines were up 5.3 percent after exchange rate effects, and up nine percent before exchange rate effects to $265.5 million, Guidant said.

"Guidant's cardiac rhythm management business continued its strong performance, while vascular intervention posted excellent stent sales internationally and is making progress in solidifying segments of our domestic dilatation product lines," said Guidant chief executive Ronald Dollens.
The medical devices maker on Monday reported first quarter earnings of $43.2 million, a 52 percent increase compared to first quarter 1996 earnings per share.
The company credited the bottom-line gain "primarily to lower interest expense, higher royalty income and a lower effective income tax rate."

Guidant added that it has been told by the Japanese Ministry of Health and Welfare that the ACS Multi-Link coronary stent system has received preliminary regulatory approval by an MHW subcommittee, an important step in the regulatory process for that country.
Guidant makes implantable defibrillators, coronary dilatation catheters and other medical products.
